newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Asia Motors union agrees to layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Asia Motors union agrees to layoffs.

text.p: Asia Motors, a unit of South Korea's Kia Group, said on Wednesday its union workers had agreed to cut the number of employees by 1,447 from 9,200.
They also agreed to let management decide wage increases for this year, a company spokesman said. Wages rose 7.8 percent last year.
"About 80 percent of union members voted for the wage issue and the layoffs," spokesman Min Jae-ki said.
Asia Motors posted a net loss of 29.4 billion won in calendar 1996 after a 8.3 billion won loss in 1995.
Min said Asia Motors' sales were expected to rise to about two trillion won this year from 1.68 trillion won in 1996.
"Exports in the first half of this year rose 22 percent from a year ago. We will begin marketing our new sport utility vehicle 'Retona' in September and this would help our sales," Min said.
